title: Cut total batch size 4x (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum 1); nothing else changed.
reflection: Negative result: val_bpb 0.998275 vs baseline 0.997359 (+0.0009). My premise was simply wrong. I assumed the baseline got ~300 optimizer steps; at 2^17 the run did 3088 steps / 405M tokens, so the baseline at 2^19 is already ~770 steps / ~420M tokens -- not step-starved at all. Two things cost us: (a) at ~770 steps the baseline is already past the point where more steps help, so 4x more steps buys nothing, and (b) per-step optimizer overhead now dominates -- steady-state MFU was only 32.5% (dt ~81ms fast steps, but many 100ms+ steps) and total tokens dropped to 405M, i.e. we paid ~4% of the token budget for the extra steps. The LR was not re-tuned for the smaller batch, so a sqrt-scaled-down LR might recover the gap, but there is no reason to think it would beat baseline -- the axis looks flat-to-slightly-bad in this direction. Useful for the group: batch size is NOT the bottleneck; the token budget is ~420M at depth 8 / 512 dim, ~1.6M tok/s, and the Muon momentum ramp (300 steps) does complete comfortably. Future runs should spend their slots on model shape (depth/width, the 4-head/128-head_dim choice) or on throughput -- 32-40% MFU on an H100 for a 50M model suggests real headroom, and every 10% throughput is ~40M extra tokens.
